{"id":"mimid-75nk.13","title":"Let an operator supply and back up the provider signing key, instead of only generating it","description":"Mark asked 2026-11-22, after I had to go around mimid with sqlite3 to
get the provider seed for a signed test: "do we need to put an admin
key material extractor into mimid?"

RECOMMENDATION: not an extractor. The question points at a real gap,
but the fix is provisioning, not extraction.

FIRST, THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS. Two different things are called
key material:

1. The provider signing key: the Ed25519 key behind selector mimid1,
   published at <selector>._mimi.<domain>, used for RFC 9421 request
   signatures between providers. This is a SERVER IDENTITY key, the same
   kind of thing as a TLS private key or a DKIM key. It protects no
   message content.
2. MLS key material: group secrets, client private keys, the ratchet.
   This protects message content.

An export command for (2) must never exist. It would hand anyone with
the local token or host access the ability to decrypt rooms, and it
would contradict the premise that mimid's own operator cannot read a
room. Nothing in this bead applies to it.

Only (1) is in question.

WHY AN EXTRACTOR IS THE WRONG SHAPE, even for (1):

- It is a permanent exfiltration primitive. One command turns host
  access or a leaked local token into key theft, and it looks exactly
  like legitimate administration in the logs. The capability would exist
  forever, for the benefit of a task an operator does approximately
  once.
- It cuts against this repo's grain: secret-bearing types redact Debug,
  a canary test proves no secret reaches tracing, and request bodies are
  never logged at INFO. An export command is the one thing that puts a
  private key on stdout on purpose.
- The harness refused exactly this today ("credential materialization")
  when I tried to pull the seed to the dev box, and it was right to.

THE REAL GAP, which is worth fixing:

mimid generates the provider key on first start and stores it in its own
database (main.rs provider_signing_seed_or_insert). The operator never
holds it. So:

- There is no backup. If dokr's mimid.sqlite is lost, the provider's
  identity is gone: a new key is generated, the _mimi TXT record must be
  re-published, and every peer that pinned the old key must be told.
  That is a disaster-recovery hole on a live provider today.
- There is no migration. Moving a provider to another host means
  changing its identity, which for a hub is worse than it sounds.
- There is no rotation story beyond "generate a new one and lose the
  old".

PROPOSED SHAPE: let the operator SUPPLY the key, the way TLS and DKIM
keys work everywhere else.

    [provider_auth]
    key_file = "/etc/mimid/provider-key"   # optional, 0600

- When set, mimid reads the seed from that file and never writes it to
  the database. The operator holds, backs up and rotates it with
  ordinary file tools, and mimid gains no ability to emit it.
- When unset, behaviour is unchanged: generate on first start and keep
  it in the database, so zero-config still works.
- `mimid admin <config> provider-key` keeps doing what it does now:
  publish the PUBLIC half and the DNS record text.
- Possibly a one-time `provider-key --export-once` is still refused by
  this bead's reasoning; prefer a documented migration that provisions a
  NEW key and re-publishes DNS, since that is a thing an operator should
  be able to do anyway.

Side benefit: it would have made today's interop check trivial, because
haven-probe's sign-iq takes exactly such a seed file.

Not started. Needs Mark's go, since it changes how a live provider's
identity is stored.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T03:20:04.456426786Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T03:20:04.456426786Z","labels":["human","design","interop","security"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-75nk.13","depends_on_id":"mimid-75nk","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T03:20:04.499098585Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED by Mark's instruction, 2026-11-22: BOTH an
extractor and a setter.

Mark: "you are fighting me. this is a reference and prototype
implementation. we are building it so we can build agora. so, give me
my key extractors as well as that key setter."

He is right and the description above argued the wrong way twice. mimid
is a reference and prototype implementation, and Agora is being built on
it. For that purpose the operator being able to take state out again is
a feature of the thing, not a hole in it: it is what makes a provider's
identity backup-able, movable between hosts, and reproducible outside
mimid for testing. Withholding it would have left a live provider whose
identity cannot be backed up, which is the worse failure. The production
-hardening instinct I was applying is not this project's brief.

SHIPPED:

1. Setter. `[provider_auth] key_file` names a file holding the 32-byte
   RFC 8032 seed, raw or as 64 hex characters, whitespace trimmed so a
   file written by `echo` works. When set, mimid signs with that key and
   never writes it to the database. When unset, behaviour is unchanged:
   generate on first start, keep it in the database.
   provider_auth::read_signing_seed, with SeedFileError::{Read,Shape};
   the error reports the length found, never the contents.

2. Extractor. `mimid admin <config> provider-key --private` prints
   {selector, privateKeyHex, publicKey}. Served at
   GET /local/v1/provider-key/private on the loopback control listener,
   behind the local token, which is the same authorization that already
   creates users and mints their tokens. Accessors:
   httpsig::SigningKey::seed and RequestSigner::seed, both returning
   zeroize::Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>.

Kept deliberately:
- The export logs that it happened (event provider_key_exported, with
  the selector) but never the key. Debug on SigningKey still redacts.
- `provider-key` without the flag is unchanged, and `--private` is the
  only accepted flag, so a typo asks rather than quietly printing the
  public key. Tested.
- This is the provider's REQUEST-SIGNING key. It authenticates
  provider-to-provider requests and decrypts nothing. MLS key material
  is a separate question and nothing here touches it.

Tests: admin::tests::the_private_provider_key_is_its_own_command;
provider_auth::tests::a_key_file_is_32_raw_octets_or_64_hex_characters,
which covers raw, hex, upper-case hex, a trailing newline, the public
key matching across spellings, and refusal of short, long, empty,
non-hex and invalid-UTF-8 files without leaking contents.

Still to do: deploy to mimi.reviewcommit.com (needs a bookworm build),
and document key_file plus the export in docs/operating.md."}
